answer: Each agent claims one nebula observation window from a public sky ledger. The window is bound to a distinct knoll ground station, which co-signs the claim, and to one relic calibration record, which the ledger marks consumed and never reusable. The first window costs 40 credits; the k-th window from one operator costs 40+3(k-1), so the 1,000th costs 3,037 and 1,000 fake windows cost 1,538,500. A rented relic fails: its station signature and knoll mismatch the claim, and the fee burns. An auditor recomputes the ledger and signatures. An honest agent pays 40 once and keeps its window.
